description: 10 ordinary-language diagnostic turns in five two-turn conversations; not reserved scores.

questions: Under the 2022 NYC building rules, an office door has a landing only 36 inches long in the direction of travel. Does that length meet the ordinary minimum?
Change the situation to a door wholly within an individual apartment. Is a 36-inch landing length allowed for that situation?
checks: No. The ordinary door-landing length in the direction of travel is at least 44 inches. Width and door-swing conditions remain separate.
Yes for this length condition. Within individual Group R-2 units the landing length need not exceed 36 inches. This does not waive width or door-swing requirements.

questions: For a new NYC bathtub, the waste outlet and overflow connect to 1-inch waste tubing. Is that size enough?
If we enlarge the tubing to 1.5 inches, can we leave out the overflow outlet?
checks: No. Bathtub waste and overflow outlets must connect to tubing or piping at least 1.5 inches in diameter.
No. Both a waste outlet and an overflow outlet are required; the waste outlet also needs a watertight stopper.

questions: Under the 2022 NYC mechanical rules, can an ordinary fuel-oil-fired appliance that takes combustion air from the bathroom be installed in that bathroom?

Suppose it is instead a direct-vent appliance taking all combustion air directly outdoors, listed for the installation and installed according to the manufacturer. Does the bathroom location exception permit it?
checks: No. Bathrooms are prohibited appliance locations unless an enumerated exception is met; the described ordinary bathroom-air appliance does not meet one.
Yes under the stated direct-vent exception in a room not used for sleeping. All combustion air must come directly outdoors, and listing and manufacturer conditions must be met.

sourceScopeNotes: Fuel oil expressly avoids treating gas-appliance location rules as Mechanical Code authority.

questions: For a new NYC natural-gas meter, may its shutoff valve be located only on the outlet side of the meter?
If we put the valve on the supply side, may we use any valve type without utility approval?
checks: No. Every meter must have a shutoff valve on the supply side.
No. Meter valves must be of a type approved by the utility company.

questions: For a NYC office sprinkler system, is a visual inspection once every three months enough for the routine visual-inspection rule?
When the monthly inspection finds a defect, does it have to appear on the inspection report?
checks: No. A visual inspection must be completed monthly by the certificate of fitness holder in accordance with NFPA 25.
Yes. All defects or violations must be noted on the inspection report.
